kaps_punt: Voedsel wat mense eet - vanaf plante en diere (klassifikasie)

items.bewering: Die kos op jou bord het nie in die winkel begin nie. Die meeste van ons kos word eers op 'n plaas gekweek of grootgemaak.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy, 'Food and Climate Infoguide' and Our World in Data 'global land for agriculture': over 40% of human calories come directly from three farmed crops (rice, wheat, maize), and meat, dairy and farmed fish together give 17%; wild-capture fish is a small, flat share (FAO data via thefern.org / humanprogress.org: about half of all fish eaten is now farmed). 'Die meeste' holds; not 'alle'.

items.bewering: Party boere kweek plante, party hou diere aan en ander doen albei.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems (2023) and Thornton & Herrero 2015 (CSIRO) on mixed crop-livestock systems in sub-Saharan Africa; Farmer's Weekly SA, 'Mixed farming: key to livestock success for Free State farmer'.

items.bewering: Ons noem hierdie werk boerdery.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: vocabulary.com 'agriculture' / 'farming': the practice of growing crops or raising animals; Merriam-Webster 'farm'.

items.bewering: Daarom kom die meeste van ons kos van plante of van diere af.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Same sources as the first item (Columbia CGEP infoguide; Our World in Data). The inference from the preceding sentences is sound, and 'die meeste' leaves room for the salt and mushrooms the lesson itself excludes later.

items.bewering: Mielies groei op 'n lang plant met groot blare.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Maize' and Britannica Kids 'corn': commercial maize about 2.5 m tall (stems 2-3 m), lower leaves 50-100 cm long and 5-10 cm wide.

items.bewering: Ons eet die pitte wat aan die mieliekop sit.
items.bron: weet.co.za 'Mielies' (Afrikaans): "'n Mieliekop bestaan uit 'n stronk, die deel waaraan die pitte vas is, en droë mielieblare"; Wikipedia 'Maize': people eat the kernels, arranged around the cob. Afrikaans usage of 'mieliekop' and 'pitte' confirmed.

items.bewering: 'n Appel is die vrug wat aan die takke van 'n appelboom groei.
items.bron: eXtension (apples.extension.org), 'What are fruiting spurs on apple trees': apples form from flowers on spurs, which are short lateral branches; Gardening Know How on spur-bearing apple trees.

items.bewering: By 'n wortel eet ons die deel van die plant wat onder die grond groei.
items.bron: NParks Singapore Flora & Fauna Web (Daucus carota): the edible part is the fleshy taproot, which grows in the soil; the green tops above ground are leaves. True on both readings of 'wortel' (carrot, or root generally).

items.bewering: Koring is 'n plant met klein korrels bo-aan sy stingel.
items.bron: Britannica Kids 'wheat': at the end of the stem is a head or spike of 20-100 tiny flowers that produce the kernels; Wikipedia 'Wheat': terminal spike.

items.bewering: Die meeste brood word van koring gemaak.
items.bron: Agricultural Product Standards Act 119 of 1990, R405 standards for wheat bread (acts.co.za): South African white and brown bread are defined as 'a dough made from white/brown wheat flour and water, with or without other ingredients'. Breads from other grains exist, so 'die meeste' is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: Daarom tel brood ook as kos van 'n plant.
items.bron: R405 standards above: the standard SA loaf is wheat flour, water and yeast, with no animal ingredient. Tested against the lesson's own groups: the minor ingredients (salt, yeast) are not animal, so bread does not move to 'albei' the way cake does, and treating it by its wheat is consistent with how the lesson treats cake and peanut butter. Some enriched breads contain milk or egg, but the sentence speaks of bread in general and follows from 'die meeste brood'.

items.bewering: Die melk wat ons drink en waarvan ons kaas en botter maak, kom van diere af.
items.bron: DALRRD 'Dairy Market Value Chain Profile 2021' (old.dalrrd.gov.za): SA milk comes from a commercial dairy herd of about 1.27 million cows; Wikipedia 'Churning (butter)' and dairy.org 'How is cheese made?' for butter and cheese being made from milk.

items.bewering: In Suid-Afrika kom hierdie melk veral van koeie.
items.bron: DALRRD 'Dairy Market Value Chain Profile 2021': four main dairy breeds (Holstein, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire), herd about 1.27 million head; Farmer's Weekly SA 'Goat milk brims with potential' and the DALRRD goat milk document: goat milk is not produced in large quantities in SA and its market is very small.

items.bewering: Vleis kom ook van diere, soos beeste, skape en hoenders.
items.bron: Farming Portal SA, 'Meat consumption in South Africa continues to surge'; Food Business MEA: poultry is about 60% of SA meat consumption, followed by beef, pork and mutton/lamb. The 'soos' list gives examples and does not claim to be complete (pork is missing but not excluded).

items.bewering: Die eiers wat ons eet, kom meestal van hoenders af.
items.bron: WATTAgNet, 'World egg output grows despite disease impact': more than 90% of world egg production is hen eggs; DALRRD 'Egg Market Value Chain Profile 2021': the SA commercial egg industry is a layer-hen industry (about 29.7 million layers).

items.bewering: Kaas groei nie self nie en word deur mense van melk gemaak.
items.bron: dairy.org 'How is cheese made?'; Wisconsin Cheese 'How is cheese made': cheese is made by people adding cultures and rennet to milk, separating the curds from the whey, then pressing and ripening.

items.bewering: Die melk kom van 'n dier soos 'n koei of 'n bok. Daarom is kaas ook kos van 'n dier.
items.bron: dairy.org (cheese from milk); Food For Mzansi, 'Turning goat milk into gold' (SA goat-milk cheese makers). 'soos' leaves room for sheep and buffalo milk. Tested with the lesson's own tracing rule: cheese leads back to milk, then to the cow or goat, so it is animal food.

items.bewering: Tog lyk die meeste kaas glad nie soos melk nie.
items.bron: dairy.org and Wisconsin Cheese on cheesemaking: the curds are separated from the liquid whey and pressed into a solid that is often ripened. Milk is a white liquid; cheese is a solid, and the hard and semi-hard yellow cheeses are also a different colour. Soft white fresh cheeses come closest, which 'die meeste' allows for.

items.bewering: Jy kan die meeste kos self in een van hierdie twee groepe sorteer.
items.bron: Tested as a set against the lesson's own exceptions, which are cake (both) and salt and mushrooms (neither). Because of 'die meeste' the sentence stays true alongside them, and the 'Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie' block repeats the same quantifier. Factual basis as in the first item (Columbia CGEP; Our World in Data).

items.bewering: Volg die kos terug tot by die plant of die dier wat dit gemaak of gegee het. As jy by 'n plant uitkom, is dit kos van 'n plant. As jy by 'n dier uitkom, is dit kos van 'n dier.
items.bron: Rule tested on every example in the lesson and on cases a learner might try. Milk and butter lead to the cow, cheese to the cow or goat, eggs to the hen and meat to the animal: all animal, correct. Bread leads to wheat, peanut butter to the peanut plant, and mielies, apples, carrots and wheat to themselves: all plant, correct. Cake leads to both, as the lesson says. Salt reaches no living thing and mushrooms reach a fungus, so neither satisfies either 'if', which agrees with the next block. A learner who already thinks a mushroom is a plant would misfile it, and that is exactly the misconception the next block corrects. Honey leads to the bee that made it, so animal, which matches the usual classification (Honey, Wikipedia for Schools / New World Encyclopedia: produced by honeybees, which change nectar with their own enzymes). Sugar leads to cane, so plant. The rule gives no false result in any case tested. Its 'gemaak of gegee' wording is what settles honey and eggs correctly.

items.bewering: Sommige kos soos koek word van plante en diere saam gemaak en kom dus van albei.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Butter cake'; Sunset 'Basic Butter Cake': the basic ingredients are flour and sugar (plant) with butter, eggs and milk (animal). 'Sommige ... soos' allows for egg-free cakes.

items.bewering: Botter word van melk gemaak en is dus kos van 'n dier.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Churning (butter)'; Dairysafe Victoria 'Butter': butter is made by churning cream or whole milk. The cream comes from the milk, so 'van melk gemaak' is accurate at this level.

items.bewering: Grondboontjiebotter word van grondboontjies gemaak en is dus kos van 'n plant.
items.bron: Peanut butter (Wikipedia): a paste made from ground dry-roasted peanuts, sometimes with added salt, sweetener or oil; peanuts are legume seeds, so they come from a plant. Added salt does not move it, by the same test as bread.

items.bewering: Die twee name klink amper dieselfde, maar die kos begin by heeltemal verskillende plekke.
items.bron: Follows from the two sourced items above: butter starts with a cow and peanut butter with a peanut plant. The comparison is about names only, and its point (that a similar name does not mean a similar source) holds.

items.bewering: Die meeste kos wat ons eet, pas in een van hierdie twee groepe. Party kos pas egter in nie een van die twee nie.
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.bron: Columbia CGEP infoguide / Our World in Data (most food from crops and livestock); the exceptions named are sourced in the next two items. Tested as a set: the plant group (mielies, apples, carrots, wheat, bread, peanut butter), the animal group (milk, cheese, butter, meat, eggs), both (cake) and neither (salt, mushrooms) have no member wrongly placed and no false contrast between them.

items.bewering: Sout kom uit die see of uit die grond en was nooit 'n plant of 'n dier nie.
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.bron: EU Salt 'Salt production': rock salt is mined, solar salt is evaporated from sea water, and vacuum salt comes from underground deposits; TxDOT and others: rock salt is the mineral halite (NaCl). Mail & Guardian, 'Salt: the journey from mine to meal' (2015): SA salt comes mostly from underground brine and inland pans in the Northern Cape/Kalahari, which counts as 'uit die grond'. Salt is a mineral, so 'nooit 'n plant of 'n dier nie' holds.

items.bewering: Sampioene lyk soos plante, maar hulle is nie plante of diere nie.
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.bron: Linnean Society, 'Discover More: Fungi' (linnean.org, 2021): Linnaeus first grouped fungi with plants, and 'we now don't consider Fungi as part of the Kingdom of Plants; they are their own Kingdom'; they do not photosynthesise and have chitin cell walls. Mapping checked: the comparison is only about appearance (which is why they were once filed with plants), and the sentence denies the classification in the same breath. It does not lead a learner further astray.

items.bewering: boerdery: Om plante te kweek, diere aan te hou of albei te doen vir kos en ander produkte.
items.bron: vocabulary.com 'agriculture': 'the practice of cultivating plants and rearing animals for food, fiber, medicinal plants, and other products'; Merriam-Webster 'farm'. Read alone, out of its block, the entry is true and complete at this level ('ander produkte' covers wool, cotton and so on).

opsomming: All 28 claims are confirmed against outside sources and nothing is uncertain. The four groups (plant, animal, both, neither) were tested as a set and have no item in the wrong place. The tracing rule gives the right answer for every example in the lesson and for honey and sugar, and the glossary entry for boerdery is true read on its own. The only thing worth a person's glance is that bread and peanut butter are classed by their main ingredient while their salt and yeast are ignored: that is consistent with the lesson's own logic and is not a false claim.
